post.caption: This purple gem comes from one place. Charoite is known from only one place, in Russia's Sakha Republic, and geologists reportedly found it in the 1940s. It was officially recognized as a mineral in the late 1970s. Its swirls come from fibrous crystals growing in interlocking patterns, and its colors range from lilac to violet. It measures 5 to 6 on the Mohs scale and is usually carved or cut into cabochons. Mining is said to be limited to about 100 tons a year, and some pieces also show a cat's-eye glow called chatoyancy. The gem is named for the Chara River, about 43 miles away.
